mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to build a house in Sydney?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on size, storeys, finishes and your site. Use our estimator for a quick guide, then book a free consultation for a fixed-price quote.

mainEntity.name: Can I build a duplex on my block?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your zoning, lot size and frontage. Many Sydney blocks qualify for a fast-track complying development (CDC) approval. We check your block for free.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between CDC and DA approval?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Complying Development Certificate (CDC) is a faster approval for designs that meet set rules. A Development Application (DA) goes through council and suits more complex designs. We advise which fits your project and manage either.

mainEntity.name: Is a knockdown rebuild cheaper than renovating?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often, yes, for older homes that need major work. You get a new home built to current standards, with no hidden structural surprises from the old house.

mainEntity.name: Do I need council approval for a granny flat?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many granny flats in NSW can be approved as complying development if the lot meets size and setback rules. We confirm this during your free consultation.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to build a new home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Timeframes depend on the design and approvals. We give you a clear schedule before construction starts.

acceptedAnswer.text: In NSW, a granny flat (secondary dwelling) is generally limited to 60 m² of internal floor area, depending on your council's rules. We confirm what your lot allows.
